Spec:
spec multiaxis_control: Shared sin/cos unit for a 16-axis motor-control loop: a 1 MHz control tick issues 32 requests at once (Park + inverse Park per axis); all 32 results must be back within 0.44 us of the tick (p99 over ticks). Max error <= 2^-12. Minimise LUTs + FFs.
  constraint: throughput_msps >= 32
  constraint: max_abs_err <= 0.000244141
  constraint: sys_p99_batch_us <= 0.44
  objective: min luts_plus_ffs (HV ref 4000)
  objective: max accuracy_bits (HV ref 12)
  select: min luts_plus_ffs
  system (simulated at L2 for the shortlist; screened at L1 by an analytic bound): control loop: a tick every 1 us issues 32 requests at once (32 requests/us on average)
  budget: 400 evals, 100/round, <= 4 rounds, eps 0.01

Evaluation budget: 400 evaluations in total, up to 100 per round,
at most 4 rounds.

Propose the first exploration plan: which families to search (1-4) and the
parameter ranges for each, with a relative budget share. Prefer families that can
plausibly meet the constraints; spend the budget where the trade-offs are. Explain
your reasoning briefly in `rationale` and per family in `why`.

families.why: Fully pipelined, 1 result/cycle, best Fmax of the two feasible families -> most margin on sys_p99_batch_us (latency N+2 plus 31 drain cycles). This is the family most likely to survive the L2 re-simulation, and it anchors the high-accuracy / high-area end of the front. W and N ranges cover the 2^-12 feasibility boundary up to ~20 accuracy bits; guards and rounding are the fine accuracy/area knobs.

Same 1 result/cycle throughput, but registers only every m stages, so it should give the smallest LUT+FF designs (the min-area corner the objective and the 4000 HV ref care about). The cost is a longer combinational path (lower Fmax) and latency ceil(N/m)+2, which eats into the 0.44 us batch budget, so m is kept moderate (2..6) to keep Fmax comfortably above the ~85-110 MHz implied by (latency+31)/0.44us. This is where the area/accuracy knee most likely lives.

parsed.rationale: The system scenario is the binding constraint: a 1 us tick dumps 32 requests at once and all 32 must be back within 0.44 us (p99). That means the unit must retire roughly one result per cycle. `iterative` needs N+3 >= 7 cycles/result and `unrolled_k` needs ceil(N/k)+3 >= 4 cycles/result, so 32 results cost >= 128-224 cycles; even at an optimistic 200-300 MHz that is 0.6-1.1 us, and their Fmax is far below that for large k/N. They also miss the 32 Msps throughput floor. So only the two fully-pipelined families (1 result/cycle) can plausibly satisfy the spec, and I spend the whole budget on them. Accuracy 2^-12 (output LSB = 2^-(W-2)) forces W >= ~15 and N >= ~13; the area objective with HV ref 4000 means the useful front runs from the minimum-area feasible corner (small W/N, minimal guards) up to ~4000 LUT+FF, so I keep W and N wide enough to reach that corner and to expose the accuracy/area knee. `pipelined_m` should win on FFs (registers every m stages instead of every stage) but loses Fmax, which directly trades against the batch-latency bound, so both families must be mapped. angle_guard/frac_guard are cheap accuracy knobs and are included on both.
